sources.title: Resumable upload protocol 1.0.x
sources.locator: Version/date lines 34-36; core HEAD/PATCH example lines 57-99; stale offset and acknowledgement lines 135-145; OPTIONS/extension advertisement lines 146-172; expiration lines 246-276; checksum lines 277-297; termination lines 327-336; concatenation/parallelism lines 350-368.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary protocol page and read the named normative sections and examples directly.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Core protocol requires HEAD to return the current Upload-Offset; PATCH offset mismatch requires 409 without changing the resource; success returns the new offset. Creation, expiration, checksum, termination, and concatenation are extensions discovered through OPTIONS/Tus-Extension. Expiration is optional; expired removed resources may return 404 or 410. Checksum validates a PATCH body, not automatically the assembled object. Termination SHOULD free associated resources.
sources.applicability: Direct basis for the Tus-facing option only. URL format, authentication, persistence, idempotent creation, whole-object verification, and backend storage are implementation choices.

sources.title: Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Multipart steps and part retry: lines 23-40; ETag/full-object checksum: lines 40-41 and 58-70; ListParts page and unfinished-part limitation: lines 51-57; checksummed consecutive part numbers: lines 64-67; KMS/SSE-C checksum requirements: lines 160-166; cleanup: lines 83-91.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact regional URL from the investigator source map, then read the primary S3 multipart sections on part identity, replacement, completion, checksums, listings, in-flight work, and permissions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Part number plus returned ETag are required for completion; a completed multipart ETag is not necessarily whole-object MD5. ListParts returns at most 1000 parts and excludes unfinished part requests; AWS says maintain the requested part-number/ETag list for completion. Reusing a part number replaces the prior part. Full-object checksums are validated server-side, but supported algorithm/type differs: AWS lists CRC64NVME, CRC32, and CRC32C as full-object, with SHA-256 in the composite table; when multipart checksums are used, part numbers must be consecutive from 1. KMS/SSE-C permissions and headers affect whether checksums are available. AWS-specific only.
sources.applicability: Evidence for Amazon S3, not the unnamed compatible service. Use to qualify the proposed boundary and identify conditions for an exact-provider test; do not generalize checksum, ETag, part, abort, or lifecycle behavior.

sources.title: Amazon S3 multipart upload limits
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the AWS limits page and read the specifications table.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS documents a 48.8 TiB maximum object, 10,000 parts, part numbers 1-10,000, parts 5 MiB-5 GiB with no minimum for the last part, and up to 1000 parts in one ListParts response.
sources.applicability: AWS limits only. The 16 MiB arithmetic in the proposal fits the stated file sizes under these AWS values; the compatible vendor remains unqualified.

sources.title: Aborting a multipart upload
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current AWS S3 User Guide page; no semantic release/version displayed; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Object is not created before successful completion and incomplete-part cost/lifecycle note, lines 4-8; abort by upload ID, lines 75-84.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the AWS abort page and read object visibility, costs, lifecycle, and abort API description.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AWS does not assemble an object until CompleteMultipartUpload succeeds; uploaded parts remain billable until complete or stop/abort; an incomplete multipart lifecycle rule can stop old uploads. After abort, the upload ID cannot upload additional parts. AWS-specific only.
sources.applicability: Supports the AWS cleanup comparison only. It does not establish equivalent semantics for the fictional compatible vendor.

sources.title: Announcement: S3 default integrity change, aws-sdk-rust issue 1240
sources.publisher: AWS SDK for Rust maintainers, awslabs/aws-sdk-rust
sources.released_version_or_commit: AWS SDK for Rust S3 client v1.69.0; issue opened 2025-01-16; no issue commit used as release identity.
sources.locator: Issue status Open and description lines 140-162.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the issue, checked status and opening date, and read the maintainer's release/default announcement and compatibility note.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: From SDK v1.69.0, S3 clients default to an additional checksum for Put calls and validation on Get calls. Maintainers caution that third-party service implementations may not yet handle newly enabled defaults; WHEN_REQUIRED options exist, though the issue says disabling integrity is not recommended.
sources.applicability: Relevant only if the gateway or another Rust component uses this AWS SDK against a compatible storage API. Supports exact endpoint/library qualification, not disabling integrity or assuming AWS-compatible semantics.
